name: Principality of Wales
alt: Principality of Wales under the English Crown

predecessors.name: Kingdom of Gwynedd
predecessors.text: Gwynedd, annexed after Dafydd's execution in 1283

predecessors.name: Deheubarth
predecessors.text: Carmarthenshire and Cardiganshire under the Justiciar of South (West) Wales

successors.name: Kingdom of England
successors.text: 'The Principality ceased to exist as a legal entity' with the Laws in Wales Acts 1535 and 1542

ledger.x: 1404: Owain Glyndwr takes Harlech and Aberystwyth.
By 1407: 'the English had recaptured Anglesey and large parts of south Wales'; Carmarthen had been taken by Owain in 1403 and by the French and Welsh in 1405.

wars.name: Welsh Revolt of 1294-1295
wars.outcome: A revolt against English rule; the Principality remained.

wars.name: Glyndwr Rising
wars.outcome: Owain proclaimed Prince of Wales 16 September 1400; most of Wales held from 1404; Aberystwyth regained by 1408, Harlech in winter 1408-1409; Owain last seen in 1412.

certainty.note: Counties were defined in 1284 by the Statute of Rhuddlan; the March frontier is soft.
